headline: Unbeaten Feyenoord go to PSV as the underdogs
summary: Feyenoord go to Eindhoven top of the Eredivisie, unbeaten after nine games on 23 points, yet the market makes PSV favourites at 47.3%, against 30.8% for Feyenoord and 21.9% for the draw. The reason is the fixture: PSV have won 3 of the last 5 meetings, including 3-0 in February. Both played in Europe this week — PSV won 1-0 at Porto, Feyenoord lost 0-1 at Real Betis. PSV are rated about 0.5 goals the better side, and over 3.75 goals has moved from 48.2% to 50.3%, after Feyenoord's last five games produced 20 goals.
read: Feyenoord arrive in Eindhoven unbeaten and top of the Eredivisie, but the market still makes PSV favourites at 47.3% — home advantage and a run of five straight PSV wins in this fixture count for more than the table. Both teams played in the Champions League in midweek, Feyenoord a day later than PSV, and the goals line is high at 3.75 with the market split almost evenly on four or more.

facts.fact: PSV are 47.3% to win at home; Feyenoord are 30.8%.
facts.meaning: The league leaders come to Eindhoven as clear underdogs — PSV's win chance is more than one and a half times Feyenoord's.

facts.fact: Feyenoord lead the Eredivisie and are unbeaten after nine games, with 23 points from seven wins and two draws.
facts.meaning: They arrive four points clear of third-placed PSV, who have already lost twice in the league.

facts.fact: PSV have won each of the last five meetings between the clubs, most recently 3-0 in Eindhoven in February.
facts.meaning: Feyenoord have taken nothing off PSV in two years, which is the backbone of PSV's favouritism.

facts.fact: Feyenoord lost 0-1 at Real Betis on Tuesday night, four days before this game.
facts.meaning: It ended a four-match winning run and leaves them with a shorter turnaround than PSV after a European away night.

facts.fact: PSV lost 1-2 at ADO Den Haag on Saturday, a third defeat in five matches in all competitions.
facts.meaning: Bosz's side have been patchy domestically while Feyenoord have swept the league unbeaten.

facts.fact: PSV won 1-0 at Porto on Tuesday, their first Champions League win of the season, with Guus Til scoring.
facts.meaning: They come into this on a European high rather than on the flat league form of the past month.

facts.fact: Feyenoord have averaged 2.19 xG per game over their last five; PSV have averaged 1.57.
facts.meaning: The away side are creating the better chances, which is why they are rated narrow outsiders rather than long ones.

facts.fact: Over 3.75 has shortened from 48.2% to 50.3% since the weekend.
facts.meaning: Four goals or more is now roughly a coin-flip on a high line of 3.75.

sources.fact: PSV Eindhoven earned their first win of this season's Champions League by beating Porto 1-0 away, with Guus Til scoring.
Peter Bosz said ahead of the Porto trip that PSV must regain consistency, stop surrendering control of matches and start turning performances into results.
Yahoo Sports described PSV's win at Porto as rewarding Peter Bosz's resilient side for their attacking persistence.
AS reported that USMNT striker Ricardo Pepi was notably absent from PSV's squad against Porto.
The Daily Record reports that 19-year-old midfielder Joel van den Berg, who made five first-team appearances for PSV, is now at Celtic and yet to debut there.
Feyenoord lost 1-0 away to Real Betis in the Champions League, with Isco scoring a penalty.

AS reports that Feyenoord brought back Giovanni van Bronckhorst, who coached the club from 2015 to 2019 and won a league title and two cups, with the aim of ending PSV's run of three straight league titles.
Feyenoord beat Como 3-2 in their Champions League match on October 14, per CBS Sports' results list.
